items.entry: CE 1938 Memorialized On the 75th Anniversary of the Battle of Gettysburg, the last Blue and Gray Reunion, a meeting of surviving Civil War veterans from the both the north and the south, is held at the park.
items.why_not_a_row: a reunion of veterans on the 75th anniversary: no memorial is named

items.entry: CE 1880 Memorialized Cultural Landscapes Inventory In c.1850 Trostle house and barn are constructed. GBMA begins to place battery guns on the battlefield to mark locations of Union batteries as early as 1880. By late 1890s, most battery locations are marked within the project area. Accompanying each is a pyramid of shells. Page 28 of 117
items.why_not_a_row: the battery guns and shell pyramids that the GBMA placed from 1880 to mark Union batteries are not named individually; the saved text of this cell also carries the page heading words inside the entry

items.entry: CE 1896 Memorialized GNPC places shell and chain fencing in front of Turnbull’s Batteries F & K and Seeley's Battery K Tablets by 1896.
items.why_not_a_row: shell and chain fencing placed in front of three tablets: the tablets are named only as the place of the fence

items.entry: CE 1897 Memorialized Stone pillars topped with shells are installed at the intersection of United States Avenue and Emmitsburg Road, and at the intersection of United States Avenue and Sickles Avenue by 1897.
